subject.title: Migration-import config merge has no prototype-pollution guard, unlike the sibling config-path writer

question: Should the public migration config patch helper drop blocked object keys, reject the affected migration item, or use another explicit failure mode when imported config contains `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`?
rationale: The vulnerability is clear, but the public SDK helper contract affects bundled and third-party migration providers, so the security boundary and user-facing failure mode need maintainer intent.

options.title: Guard shared SDK helper
options.body: Block prototype-bearing keys in `mergeMigrationConfigValue` and `writeMigrationConfigPath`, with regression coverage for direct helper behavior and Hermes-imported provider, MCP, and skill keys.

options.title: Sanitize only Hermes imports
options.body: Filter Hermes provider, MCP, and skill keys locally, fixing the reported bundled path while leaving the shared SDK helper behavior unchanged for other providers.

options.title: Document trusted import input
options.body: Leave migration imports unchanged and treat tampered prior-tool configs as out of scope, accepting the current prototype-write primitive.

recommendation.title: Guard shared SDK helper
recommendation.body: Block prototype-bearing keys in `mergeMigrationConfigValue` and `writeMigrationConfigPath`, with regression coverage for direct helper behavior and Hermes-imported provider, MCP, and skill keys.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the migration provider/onboarding helper path and is the clearest routing owner for the SDK helper boundary decision.
